newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Iran delivers first oil under swap with Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: Iran delivers first oil under swap with Kazakhstan.

text.p: Iran has made its first delivery of Gulf oil to clients of energy-rich but landlocked Kazakhstan, in a much-delayed oil swap deal with the former Soviet republic, Russia's Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.

Citing the state-owned Kazakh Oil company, which conducts the Central Asian state's oil policy, the agency said 67,500 tonnes of Iraqi crude was made available to Kazakhstan at the Gulf at the weekend.
Last month, Kazakh Oil chief Nurlan Balgimbayev said the Iranians would deliver around 70,000 tonnes of oil at Kharg Island.
Kazakhstan began shipping crude across the Caspian Sea to northern Iran last December.

Under the deal, which Balgimbayev said could total around one million tonnes of oil this year and up to five million tonnes annually in the next six years, Iran must provide the equivalent amount of crude at its Gulf ports for Kazakh clients.
The swap had been delayed earlier this year over sulphur impurities, called mercaptans, in Kazakh crude, which the Iranians said they were unable to refine.
Kazakhstan is anxious to break is dependence on a Soviet era pipeline network controlled by Russia for its oil exports.
